|website=HoopsHype |publisher=HoopsHype}} earning seven [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive Team]] selections and winning [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|Defensive Player of the Year]] honors in [[2014–15 NBA season#Yearly Awards|2015]] and [[2015–16 NBA season#Yearly Awards|2016]]. In 2021, he was named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]]. Leonard played two seasons of [[college basketball]] for [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]]. He was selected 15th overall by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]] before being traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on draft night. With the Spurs, Leonard won an NBA championship in [[2014 NBA Finals|2014]] and was named the [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award|Finals Most Valuable Player]]. After seven seasons with the Spurs, Leonard was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2018. In his only season with the Raptors in [[2019 NBA Playoffs|2019]], he led the Raptors to their first NBA championship and won his second Finals MVP award (one of only three players to win Finals MVP with multiple teams, along with [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] and [[LeBron James]]). He subsequently moved to his hometown of [[Los Angeles]] and signed with the Clippers as a free agent in July 2019. In 2021, Leonard led them to their first conference finals appearance in franchise history. Leonard was awarded [[Associated Press Athlete of the Year]] in 2019.{{cite web |last1=Reynolds |first1=Tim |title=Former Raptors star Kawhi Leonard is AP's male athlete of 2019 {{!}} CBC Sports |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/toronto-raptors-la-clippers-nba-ap-kawhi-leonard-athlete-of-the-year-1.5409353 |website=CBC |access-date=July 10, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260710082848/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/toronto-raptors-la-clippers-nba-ap-kawhi-leonard-athlete-of-the-year-1.5409353 |archive-date=July 10, 2026 |date=December 27, 2019}} ==Early life== Leonard attended [[Canyon Springs High School (Moreno Valley, California)|Canyon Springs High School]] in [[Moreno Valley, California]], before transferring to [[Martin Luther King High School (Riverside, California)|Martin Luther King High School]] for his junior year.{{cite web |title=OSDB - Kawhi Leonard - LA Clippers |url=https://www.osdbsports.com/nba/players/kawhi-leonard/biography/c12fb587-fc86-471c-8a84-19caf31325ce |access-date=February 3, 2024 |website=osdbsports.com |archive-date=February 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240203031000/https://www.osdbsports.com/nba/players/kawhi-leonard/biography/c12fb587-fc86-471c-8a84-19caf31325ce |url-status=live}} In his senior year there, he and [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]] led the King High Wolves to a 30–3 record. [[Aspiration, Inc.|Aspiration]] in 2021. Investigative sportswriter [[Pablo Torre (journalist)|Pablo Torre]] reported that Leonard had signed a $28 million "no-show" endorsement deal with Aspiration which had not required any action on Leonard's part, other than remaining a Clipper. Torre cited anonymous former employees of the company to allege that Leonard's deal with the company, in which Clippers' owner [[Steve Ballmer]] had invested $50 million, was a means of paying Leonard under the table to circumvent the NBA salary cap.{{cite news |last1=Vardon |first1=Joe |last2=Amick |first2=Sam |date=September 4, 2025 |title=Kawhi Leonard, Clippers used endorsement deal to |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331}} John Karalis of the Boston Sports Journal later reported that Leonard also received an additional $20 million in Aspiration company stock, bringing Leonard's total promised compensation from the company to $48 million.{{cite web |last1=Karalis |first1=John |title=BSJ Exclusive: Kawhi Leonard endorsement deal that triggered NBA investigation was actually worth $48 million |url=https://www.bostonsportsjournal.com/2025/09/04/exclusive-kawhi-leonard-endorsement-deal-that-triggered-nba-investigation-actually-worth-48-million |access-date=September 6, 2025 |website=BostonSportsJournal.com |date=September 4, 2025}} The NBA responded by announcing it was investigating the matter.{{cite web |title=NBA says it will open investigation into report that Clippers broke cap rules with Leonard deal |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-kawhi-leonard-investigation-6fd39c215edea2f2945c85fad63c9c80 |access-date=September 6, 2025 |website=AP News
